ev.rus_m_banya.text: Saturday bathhouse: the grown-ups whip you with a birch whisk until you are red as a boiled crayfish, and then you leap shrieking into a snowdrift and run back to the steam bench.
ev.rus_m_ice_hill.text: For Maslenitsa they poured water down the slope to make an ice hill. You fly down on a sled of frozen dung and straw, knock over three other children and laugh louder than any of them.
ev.rus_m_kolyada.text: At Yuletide you go round the yards with the mummers: sheepskin coat turned inside out, soot on your cheeks, carols under the windows. Housewives drop pies and little cow-shaped cookies into your sack.
ev.rus_m_kupala.text: On Kupala night you {g:leapt over the bonfire with the lads and hunted for the fern flower until dawn|floated a wreath down the river and watched which bank it drifted to}. The priests scold these games, but all the young people come down to the river.
ev.rus_m_onfim.text: The teacher gave you a strip of birch bark and a bone stylus. You scratched out the alphabet, and on the back yourself on horseback spearing an enemy. The bark was later thrown into the mud of the street, and there it will lie for a very long time.
ev.rus_m_stove.text: In winter you sleep on top of the stove. Below, a pine splinter crackles for light, cockroaches rustle behind the chimney, and an old neighbour who came in to warm up tells tales of Baba Yaga so frightening that it is delicious.
ev.rus_m_mushrooms.text: You were taken to the forest for mushrooms and lingonberries. You filled your basket, then saw a bear's print the size of a sieve by the ravine, and ran home faster than anyone.
ev.rus_m_icon_corner.text: In the icon corner of the cottage a little lamp flickers before a dark icon. You are taught to cross yourself with two fingers, to bow from the waist and never to point at the holy image.
ev.rus_m_haymaking.text: Haymaking. The whole village is on the meadow from dawn: scythes ring, women turn the hay with rakes, and at noon there is cold kvass from the jug and a song that carries across the river.
ev.rus_m_easter_bells.text: Easter night: the procession with candles, "Christ is risen!", and every bell tower ringing at once. All through Bright Week anyone may climb up and ring. You rang until you were half deaf.
ev.rus_m_podil.text: At the Podil landing the boats are unloading: Greeks with silks and wine in clay jars, Varangians with swords, Bulgars with silver, and local men with furs, wax and slaves for sale.
ev.rus_m_veche_bell.text: The veche bell rang on Yaroslav's Court. The Trade Side has fallen out with the St Sophia Side again: they shouted themselves hoarse, and it ended with somebody thrown off the Great Bridge into the Volkhov.
ev.rus_m_bridge_dive.text: The boys dive into the Volkhov from the Great Bridge. You jumped too, feet first with your eyes squeezed shut, and came up right under the nose of a boatman, who swore at you long and colourfully.
ev.rus_m_white_stone.text: Stonecutters are carving white limestone for the new cathedral: lions, griffins, King David with his harp. You stand and watch for ages as beasts nobody here has ever seen emerge from the stone.
ev.rus_m_fryagi.text: Italian masters from beyond the sea are building new red-brick walls for the Kremlin: battlements shaped like swallowtails and towers taller than any church. The Moscow brickmakers grumble, but they learn.
ev.rus_m_winter_road.text: The winter road: the convoy travels on the river ice, because in summer there is no way through the marshes. Frost burns your face, the horses are white with rime, and you sleep by a fire on the bank, back to back.
ev.rus_m_honeycomb.text: The beekeeper climbed down from a pine and broke you off a piece of honeycomb. Honey ran down your chin, a bee stung your lip and it swelled up for half the day, but the honey was worth it.
ev.rus_m_bliny.text: For Maslenitsa you bake pancakes from morning till night. The first one comes out lumpy, as always, and is set aside for the dead. The rest are eaten before they can cool.
ev.rus_m_posidelki.text: An evening gathering: the girls have brought their distaffs to one cottage, sing long slow songs and pretend not to notice the lads peering in at the little window.
ev.rus_m_fistfight.text: A fist fight on the ice: street against street, wall against wall. You don't hit a man who is down, and you don't hide lead in your mitten, or so they say. You came home with a black eye and very pleased with yourself.
ev.rus_m_wolves.text: All night wolves howled at the edge of the village. The dogs strained at their chains and the cow thrashed in the byre. In the morning a neighbour was one sheep short.
ev.rus_m_ice_break.text: The ice is breaking! The river cracks its ice with a roar, the floes pile up on the bank. A week later the spring flood reached the lower streets, and people rowed boats along them.
ev.rus_m_lent.text: Great Lent: seven weeks of radish, sauerkraut, mushrooms and bread. The milk goes to the calves, and by Easter the whole street is thin, quiet and thinking about Easter cake.
ev.rus_m_easter_eggs.text: At Easter everyone exchanges the Easter kiss and gives dyed eggs. You rolled eggs down a wooden chute and won five whole eggs from the neighbours' children.
ev.rus_m_domovoy.text: At night something rustles and sighs behind the stove. The grown-ups say it is the house spirit and leave him a little pot of porridge in the corner. In the morning the pot is empty. You are fairly sure it was the cat, but not entirely.
ev.rus_m_skomorokhi.text: Skomorokhi, the wandering players, came to the market: a fiddle, a tambourine, a puppeteer behind a screen and a bear that bows to the boyars and shows how the village women go to fetch water.
ev.rus_m_baskak.text: A Horde tax officer rode down the street with his horsemen. Everyone fell silent, took off their caps and stared at the ground until the hoofbeats faded. For a long time afterwards nobody spoke above a murmur.
ev.rus_m_sledge.text: A sledge ride: rugs in the sleigh, bells under the shaft-bow, snow flying up from the hooves into your face. The driver whistles and villages flash by as if in a fairy tale.
ev.rus_m_kaliki.text: Wandering pilgrims sat down at the gate, blind men with staffs. They sing a holy verse about Alexius, the Man of God, so movingly that the women weep and the men turn away.
ev.rus_m_kholop_feast.text: At the master's feast you stand by the door with a ladle. The gusli player sings of Ilya Muromets, the boyars roar with laughter, and towards morning you get half a loaf and a swan's wing.
ev.rus_m_glow.text: At night a red glow rose over the far end of town: another fire. Until dawn you stood at the gate with a bucket, watching which way the wind would turn.
ev.rus_m_old_tales.text: The neighbours' children climb onto the bench and beg for stories of the old days. You tell them, and are surprised yourself at how much you have seen.
ev.rus_m_german_court.text: Hanseatic merchants in long coats stand outside the German Court. They speak their own tongue, lock the yard at night and let loose the dogs, and their cloth makes the boyars' wives gasp.
ev.rus_m_monastery_bread.text: The monastery hands out bread to the poor in memory of someone's soul. You got a slice too, warm and with caraway, and kept it inside your shirt for a long time to make the pleasure last.
ev.rus_m_sour_cabbage.text: In autumn the whole street chops cabbage, and the thud of choppers carries all the way to the river. The tubs go down to the cellar, and the children get the cores, the best treat of the month.
ev.rus_d_polyudye.title: The Tribute Round
ev.rus_d_polyudye.text: In winter the prince and his retinue tour the land collecting tribute. The retainers demand furs, honey and wax from every household. You could hide some of the pelts in the barn.
ev.rus_d_polyudye.hide.success: The retainers didn't bother with the barn. You will get through the winter with something to spare.
ev.rus_d_polyudye.hide.failure: They found the pelts. They took twice as much and gave you a taste of the whip besides.
ev.rus_d_polyudye.note: Polyudye was the prince's yearly circuit of his lands to gather tribute. In 945 Prince Igor was killed by the Drevlians when he tried to collect a second time; afterwards Princess Olga put the collection on a fixed footing.
ev.rus_d_vira.title: The Community Fine
ev.rus_d_vira.text: A murdered man was found on your community's land. The killer was not found, and by the law the whole commune owes the prince a blood fine. The elders are dividing the share among the households.
ev.rus_d_vira.search.success: You found the stranger's trail and brought witnesses. The commune pays nothing, and people bow to you.
ev.rus_d_vira.search.failure: The trail went cold. Time was lost, and your share turned out even larger.
ev.rus_d_vira.note: The Russkaya Pravda, a law code begun under Yaroslav the Wise, made the whole verv, the rural commune, pay a "wild fine" if a body was found on its land and the killer was not found.
ev.rus_d_zakup.title: The Loan
ev.rus_d_zakup.text: After a bad harvest the bins are empty. The boyar's steward offers a kupa, a loan of grain and silver, to be repaid by working the boyar's fields. Such people are called zakupy, and they live almost like slaves.
ev.rus_d_zakup_later.title: No Way Out for a Zakup
ev.rus_d_zakup_later.text: For years you have worked off the loan, yet the debt never shrinks: the steward charges you for trampled crops, for a broken plough. Neighbours whisper that you could run away, but by law a runaway zakup becomes a full slave.
ev.rus_d_zakup_later.buyout: Pay off the rest in silver
ev.rus_d_zakup_later.flee: Flee at night to another land
ev.rus_d_zakup_later.flee.success: You slipped through the forests into another principality. Nobody there asks where you came from.
ev.rus_d_zakup_later.flee.failure: They caught you on the third day. Now you are a full slave, for good.
ev.rus_d_terem.title: The Terem
ev.rus_d_terem.text: Girls of good family are kept in the terem, the upper rooms: embroider, pray, never show yourself to strangers. From the little window you can see the whole market, and today there are foreign envoys with elephants... well, camels at least.
ev.rus_d_terem.peek.success: You saw the envoys, the camels and half of Moscow, and got back unnoticed.
ev.rus_d_terem.peek.failure: Your nurse caught you. Word went round every terem that you are a shameless girl.
ev.rus_d_pilgrimage.title: To the Trinity Monastery
ev.rus_d_pilgrimage.text: The neighbours are setting off on foot to the Trinity monastery founded by St Sergius. It is a week's walk, sleeping wherever you can, but people come back with shining faces.
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery.title: A Gift for the Soul
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery.text: The abbot reminds you: whoever gives the monastery a village will be remembered at every service, you and your whole line, for as long as the monastery stands.
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery.village: Sign a village over to the monastery
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery.silver: Give what silver you can spare
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery.refuse: The land is for the living
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery_later.title: The Monastery Remembers
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery_later.text: You passed the monastery you once endowed. The monks recognised you, brought out bread and said your name is read from their book of remembrance at every liturgy. In a hard year the monastery is ready to help you too.
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery_later.visit: Stay for the service with the brethren
ev.rus_d_gift_monastery_later.ask: Ask for a loan from the monastery's treasury
ev.rus_d_yuriev.title: St George's Day
ev.rus_d_yuriev.text: St George's Day in autumn: for a week before and a week after, a peasant may leave his landlord for another, once he pays the "dwelling fee". A neighbouring landholder promises three years free of dues.
ev.rus_d_yuriev.leave.success: The new master kept his word. The land is better here and the dues are lighter.
ev.rus_d_yuriev.leave.failure: They gave you the relief, but the land is nothing but stones. You were cheated.
ev.rus_d_yuriev.stay: Stay: better the devil you know
ev.rus_d_yuriev.note: The law code of 1497 limited peasant moves to the week before and after St George's Day in autumn (26 November), with a fee. From 1581 "forbidden years" banned moving altogether, a step towards serfdom.
ev.rus_d_kormlenie.title: A Feeding Post
ev.rus_d_kormlenie.text: The grand prince has granted you a "feeding": for a year or two you govern a district town and live on what the locals pay you, the arrival gift, holiday dues and court fees.
ev.rus_d_kormlenie.fair: Take what custom allows, no more
ev.rus_d_kormlenie.note: Under the feeding system governors were maintained by the people they ruled. Abuses were constant; in 1555–56 Ivan IV abolished feedings and replaced them with local self-government.
ev.rus_d_kormlenie_later.title: A Petition Against You
ev.rus_d_kormlenie_later.text: The townspeople you once "fed" on have reached Moscow with a petition listing everything down to the last hen. A clerk hints that the matter can be settled by giving it back.
ev.rus_d_kormlenie_later.deny.success: The witnesses got muddled and the boyars waved the matter away.
ev.rus_d_kormlenie_later.deny.failure: You were found out. The fine is heavy and your name is in the mud.
ev.rus_d_mestnichestvo.title: Precedence
ev.rus_d_mestnichestvo.text: At the sovereign's feast you were seated below a man whose ancestors served below yours. Sit down, and your whole line loses honour for generations. Refuse, and you may anger the sovereign.
ev.rus_d_mestnichestvo.refuse: "It is beneath my rank to sit below him!"
ev.rus_d_mestnichestvo.refuse.success: The service registers were checked: you were right. You were moved up the table.
ev.rus_d_mestnichestvo.refuse.failure: The sovereign was angered. You were "handed over by the head" to your rival, a disgrace before the whole court.
ev.rus_d_mestnichestvo.note: Mestnichestvo was the system by which a man's post in service and seat at table depended on his lineage and his ancestors' service. Disputes over "places" were constant; it was abolished in 1682.
ev.rus_d_veche.title: The Veche
ev.rus_d_veche.text: The prince has broken his compact with Novgorod and is putting his own men in charge of the districts. The veche bell booms: "We don't want this prince, let him be gone!" Some shout to expel him, others fear war with his kin.
ev.rus_d_veche.expel.success: The veche decided: the prince goes. You were in the front rank.
ev.rus_d_veche.expel.failure: It came to fists, and you were crushed in the throng.
ev.rus_d_veche.note: The Novgorod veche was a town assembly that from 1136 invited and expelled princes and elected the posadnik, the tysyatsky and even the archbishop. Its bell was carted off to Moscow in 1478.
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.title: A Letter to a Debtor
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.text: A neighbour has owed you for two years. You could scratch him a note on birch bark, "Pay what you owe me or I'll send the bailiffs", the way everyone does here. Or go straight to the posadnik's court.
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.letter.success: Three days later he brought the silver and begged you not to shame him before the whole street.
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.letter.failure: He read it, spat and threw the bark into the mud.
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.court: Take him to the posadnik's court
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.court.success: The court awarded you the debt with a penalty.
ev.rus_d_birch_debt.court.failure: You had no witnesses. The case was put off indefinitely.
ev.rus_d_hansa.title: The German Court
ev.rus_d_hansa.text: A Hanseatic merchant from the German Court will take wax and squirrel pelts in bulk and pay in Flemish cloth. They test the wax by driving a knife into every cake: mix in tallow and you are finished.
ev.rus_d_hansa.deal.success: The cloth went to boyars' wives at three times the price. A good year.
ev.rus_d_hansa.deal.failure: The German found tallow in one cake of wax, your supplier's doing, and broke off the deal.
ev.rus_d_hansa.small: Sell a little at a time, no risk
ev.rus_d_ordeal.title: Trial by Iron
ev.rus_d_ordeal.text: A neighbour accuses you of stealing a horse. There are no witnesses, and the judge rules by the law: "Give him the iron." Whoever carries red-hot iron and heals cleanly is in the right.
ev.rus_d_ordeal.iron.success: The burn healed cleanly. Your accuser pays you for the insult.
ev.rus_d_ordeal.iron.failure: Your hand festered. The court found you guilty.
ev.rus_d_ordeal.witnesses: Find witnesses who saw you that night
ev.rus_d_ordeal.witnesses.success: Two neighbours vouched for you. The case is closed.
ev.rus_d_ordeal.witnesses.failure: Nobody wanted to get involved. You had to pay.
ev.rus_d_ordeal.pay: Pay him off to be rid of it
ev.rus_d_skomorokh.title: The Players' Band
ev.rus_d_skomorokh.text: The wandering players are leaving the village and want you along: you have a voice and nimble hands. You would roam from town to town with a fiddle and a bear. Priests call players the devil's servants, but everyone laughs at their jokes.
ev.rus_d_skomorokh_later.title: Time to Settle?
ev.rus_d_skomorokh_later.text: Years on the road: you know a hundred songs and how to make the gloomiest boyar laugh. But your back aches and the bear has grown old. In one town a craftsman you know is willing to take you into his trade.
ev.rus_d_skomorokh_later.settle: Settle down and learn a trade
ev.rus_d_skomorokh_later.roam: One more season on the road
ev.rus_d_polon_ransom.title: The Captives
ev.rus_d_polon_ransom.text: Captives taken by the steppe raiders last summer are being driven through town for resale. Among them is a girl from the village across the river. The merchants will release her for a ransom.
ev.rus_d_polon_ransom.collect: Collect a little from each neighbour
ev.rus_d_icon_order.title: An Icon for a Vow
ev.rus_d_icon_order.text: You made a vow: if the trouble passed, you would give an icon to your parish church. The trouble has passed. A good icon painter charges a lot and takes months, while the market sells cheap "everyday" icons, quick and inexpensive.
ev.rus_d_pravezh.title: Pravezh
ev.rus_d_pravezh.text: Your debt is overdue and you are put on pravezh: every morning outside the government office debtors are beaten on the shins until they pay. You can sell everything, or sign yourself into bondage to the lender.
ev.rus_d_pravezh.pay: Sell what you have and pay
ev.rus_d_pravezh.note: Pravezh was debt collection by corporal punishment, common in the Muscovite state in the 16th and 17th centuries. A debtor could also become a lender's "bonded kholop", working off the debt.
ev.rus_d_bratchina.title: The Brotherhood Feast
ev.rus_d_bratchina.text: For the parish feast day the neighbours brew beer and mead together, a bratchina. Whoever pays a share is a brother: at the common table they settle disputes, reconcile enemies and choose the elder.
ev.rus_d_salt.title: The Saltworks
ev.rus_d_salt.text: In the north, at Sol Galitskaya and Solvychegodsk, brine is pumped from the ground and boiled down in huge iron pans. Every household needs salt. Merchants you know are building a new saltworks and looking for partners.
ev.rus_d_salt_later.title: The Salt Is Flowing
ev.rus_d_salt_later.text: The saltworks you invested in is finally producing. The partners are counting profits and arguing: split them now, or sink another brine pipe.
ev.rus_d_salt_later.take.success: The salt went down the Sukhona and the Dvina, and your share turned out handsome.
ev.rus_d_salt_later.take.failure: The brine weakened, and the profit was modest.
ev.rus_d_hunger_bondage.title: A Hungry Spring
ev.rus_d_hunger_bondage.text: By spring the grain is gone. People mix goosefoot and ground pine bark into the flour. A boyar is taking people in "for bread", as slaves of their own free will. You would not starve, but you would not be free.
ev.rus_d_hunger_bondage.bondage: Go into the boyar's service as a kholop
ev.rus_d_hunger_bondage.endure: Hold out until the new harvest
ev.rus_d_marry_kholop.title: Love Across the Line
ev.rus_d_marry_kholop.text: You have fallen in love with {g:a girl|a young man} who is a kholop on a boyar's estate. By law, whoever marries a kholop without an agreement with the master becomes a kholop too. The master will free {g:her|him}, for a ransom.
ev.rus_d_marry_kholop.marry: Marry without an agreement, come what may
ev.rus_d_umykanie.title: Games by the Water
ev.rus_d_umykanie.text: At the games between villages, with dancing and songs, the lads "carry off" their brides, with the girls' consent, of course. The girl you've been exchanging glances with all evening has nodded towards the dark riverbank.
ev.rus_d_umykanie.steal.success: By morning you are husband and wife by the old custom. Her family can only join the feast.
ev.rus_d_umykanie.steal.failure: Her brothers had not been told about the arrangement. You barely got away.
ev.rus_d_umykanie.note: The Primary Chronicle says that some early Slavic tribes "carried off" wives at games between villages, by agreement with the bride. The Church fought the custom.
ev.rus_t_polon.title: The Raid
ev.rus_t_polon.text: At dawn there is smoke over the next village and the drum of hooves. Steppe riders are sweeping the country, seizing people and cattle. The forest is across a field; the town is a day away.
ev.rus_t_polon.hide: Run for the forest and the marshes
ev.rus_t_polon.hide.success: You spent three days in the marsh. Your home burned, but you are alive.
ev.rus_t_polon.hide.failure: The dogs found you. A rope around your neck and a long road south into captivity.
ev.rus_t_polon.fight: Take up an axe and defend the yard
ev.rus_t_polon.fight.success: The raiders pulled back rather than fight. People will tell stories about you.
ev.rus_t_polon.fight.failure: You were struck down and bound. You came to in a column of captives.
ev.rus_t_polon.flee_town: Leave everything and run for the capital
ev.rus_t_polon_return.title: Ransomed from Captivity
ev.rus_t_polon_return.text: The years of captivity are over: the metropolitan's men bought back a group of captives at a slave market, and you among them. You are being taken home, though home may no longer exist.
ev.rus_t_hoard.title: The Hoard
ev.rus_t_hoard.text: The plough caught on a pot. Inside is silver: eastern coins with strange writing, neck rings, bits of bracelets. Someone buried it long ago and never came back.
ev.rus_t_hoard.prince: Take it to the prince's steward
ev.rus_t_hoard.church: Give part of it to the church
ev.rus_t_hoard_informer.title: Someone Saw
ev.rus_t_hoard_informer.text: A neighbour walks in without knocking and sits on the bench: "I saw what you dug up back then, you know. Shall I tell the steward?"
ev.rus_t_hoard_informer.refuse.success: He never went to the steward, afraid of being questioned himself.
ev.rus_t_hoard_informer.refuse.failure: The steward came with his men and took nearly everything.
ev.rus_t_opala.title: Disgrace
ev.rus_t_opala.text: The sovereign has put you in disgrace: someone informed that you were in contact with the King of Lithuania. Your estate is being taken for the crown and you are barred from court. Friends no longer recognise you in the street.
ev.rus_t_opala.lithuania.success: You crossed the border. The Lithuanian king received you, but your homeland is gone.
ev.rus_t_opala.lithuania.failure: You were caught at the border. Everything you owned went to the treasury.
ev.rus_t_opala.beg: Bow to the ground and beg for mercy
ev.rus_t_opala.beg.success: The metropolitan interceded. The sovereign relented, but kept part of your land.
ev.rus_t_opala.beg.failure: Your petition was refused. You are now a serviceman without an estate.
ev.rus_t_city_fire.title: Fire
ev.rus_t_city_fire.text: The town is burning. The wind carries brands across the street and the wooden roofs catch one after another. Your yard is next.
ev.rus_t_city_fire.goods.success: You saved the chests and the icons. The house burned, but you can build another.
ev.rus_t_city_fire.goods.failure: The roof came down before you could get out. Burns, and almost nothing saved.
ev.rus_t_city_fire.neighbors.success: You carried two children out of the smoke. Their father is your friend for life.
ev.rus_t_city_fire.neighbors.failure: The children were saved, but you were carried out unconscious and badly burned.
ev.rus_t_city_fire.tear_down: Pull down the next cabin to stop the fire
ev.rus_t_ushkuiniki.title: The River Raiders
ev.rus_t_ushkuiniki.text: Bold young Novgorodians are fitting out ushkuis, light river boats, and calling men to go down the Volga to the rich towns. Boyars put up silver for the gear and expect a share. The veche will later say it knew nothing about it.
ev.rus_t_ushkuiniki.join.success: You came back with silver and cloth. Better not to tell the priest about it.
ev.rus_t_ushkuiniki.join.failure: The band was beaten outside a foreign town. You came back barely alive.
ev.rus_t_witch.title: Whispers Behind Your Back
ev.rus_t_witch.text: A third year of bad harvests, and the village is looking for someone to blame. They whisper that you "hold back the bounty" by witchcraft: you know herbs and keep to yourself. The men are already giving you dark looks.
ev.rus_t_witch.church.success: The priest gave you communion before everyone and shamed the loudmouths.
ev.rus_t_witch.church.failure: The priest defended you half-heartedly. The rumour didn't die, and people stopped greeting you.
ev.rus_t_witch.stand: Face them at the village meeting
ev.rus_t_witch.stand.success: You reminded them whom you had healed and whose children you had nursed. The shouters fell silent.
ev.rus_t_witch.stand.failure: The crowd was angrier than words. You were beaten, and only a neighbour stepped in in time.
ev.rus_t_prince_hunt.title: The Prince's Hunt
ev.rus_t_prince_hunt.text: Towards evening a rider in a rich cloak came out of the woods to your yard, separated from the hunt and lost. From his rings and the way his young retainers came running after him, it is clear: this is the prince himself.
ev.rus_t_prince_hunt.host: Receive him as an honoured guest
ev.rus_t_prince_hunt.host.success: The prince remembered you and sent gifts. Now you have a protector at court.
ev.rus_t_prince_hunt.host.failure: The prince ate, thanked you and rode away. You never saw him again.
ev.rus_t_prince_hunt.humble: Show him the way and bow
ev.rus_t_tonsure.title: The Veil
ev.rus_t_tonsure.text: You have no children, and your husband plans to have you veiled as a nun so he can marry again. It has happened even in the greatest houses, even to a grand prince's wife. Your relatives whisper: agree, or it will go worse for you.
ev.rus_t_tonsure.resist.success: The metropolitan refused to allow the divorce. You remain mistress of the house.
ev.rus_t_tonsure.resist.failure: You were veiled by force. They say you wept and cried out in the church.
ev.rus_t_far_trade.title: Beyond Three Seas
ev.rus_t_far_trade.text: Merchants are gathering a caravan down the Volga to Sarai and Shemakha, and the boldest beyond, across the sea. The profits there are fabulous. But not everyone comes back.
ev.rus_t_far_trade.go.success: You came back with silk, pepper and stories nobody believes.
ev.rus_t_far_trade.go.failure: Near Astrakhan the caravan was robbed. You came back penniless and sick, but alive.
ev.rus_t_far_trade_later.title: Notes on a Journey
ev.rus_t_far_trade_later.text: You are being asked to travel far again, and young merchants beg you to describe the road: where the tolls are, where the robbers lurk, where you can trust no one. Perhaps you should write it all down while you still remember?
ev.rus_t_far_trade_later.write: Write down your journey for others
ev.rus_t_stroganov.title: East to the Stroganovs
ev.rus_t_stroganov.text: The Stroganov merchants have a charter from the tsar for the empty lands along the Kama and the Chusovaya and are calling free men to boil salt, trap sable and build forts. Beyond lie the Ural Mountains, and past them, Siberia.
ev.rus_t_stroganov.go.success: The first winter was terrible, the second rich. The forests here are full of sable.
ev.rus_t_stroganov.go.failure: Scurvy and frost almost killed you in the very first winter.
ev.rus_t_don.title: To the Don
ev.rus_t_don.text: Word goes round in whispers: on the Don live the free Cossacks, who never hand runaways back. "From the Don there is no return." The road across the Wild Field is long, and runaways who are caught are sent back and flogged.
ev.rus_t_don.flee.success: You made it. The Cossack circle accepted you, and now you are your own master, and a fighter.
ev.rus_t_don.flee.failure: You were caught by the Oka and sent back. Your back remembers the whip.
ev.rus_j_monk_copy.title: Copying a Book
ev.rus_j_monk_copy.text: The abbot has ordered a copy of the Acts and Epistles for a new church. Parchment is precious, the ink is made from oak galls, the letters must stand as straight as soldiers. In the margin you are dying to add: "Oh, my hand hurts."
ev.rus_j_monk_copy.note: Add in the margin: "Forgive me, brethren, a lazy sinner wrote this"
ev.rus_j_monk_hegumen.title: {g:Abbot|Abbess}
ev.rus_j_monk_hegumen.text: The old {g:abbot|abbess} has died, and the community asks you to lead the house: the estates, the villages, the lawsuits with neighbouring boyars and a hundred souls on your conscience.
ev.rus_j_icon_commission.title: The Deesis Tier
ev.rus_j_icon_commission.text: The bishop is commissioning a whole tier of icons for the cathedral: Christ in Majesty, the Mother of God, the Forerunner, the apostles. The deadline is the Feast of the Protection. You can take it on yourself or work as an assistant to a famous master.
ev.rus_j_icon_commission.accept.success: The bishop stood silently before your Christ for a long time. Then he ordered you paid double.
ev.rus_j_icon_commission.accept.failure: You didn't finish in time: the paint wouldn't dry in the damp and the faces came out flat. You were paid half.
ev.rus_j_icon_workshop.title: A Workshop of Your Own
ev.rus_j_icon_workshop.text: Apprentices are asking to join you: grinding pigments, boiling glue, preparing panels. With a team you could take big commissions, whole churches. But you would have to feed the team.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_bear.title: A Bear at the Hive
ev.rus_j_bortnik_bear.text: A bear has reached your best hive: it is hugging the pine and climbing towards the hollow while the bees swarm in a cloud. You could drive it off with a boar spear, or walk away and lose the honey.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_bear.fight.success: The bear left. And the hide of another one is on your bench now, or so you tell everyone.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_bear.fight.failure: The bear was quicker. They found you under the pine, badly mauled.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_sign.title: The Felled Hive Tree
ev.rus_j_bortnik_sign.text: A neighbour has cut down a pine bearing your hive mark. By law, damaging a hive tree carries a fine. But the neighbour swears he never saw the mark.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_sign.sue.success: The mark could be seen from far off: the court awarded you the fine.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_sign.sue.failure: The neighbour brought witnesses who said the pine belonged to no one.
ev.rus_j_bortnik_sign.peace: Make peace over a ladle of mead
ev.rus_j_trapper_sable.title: Black Sable
ev.rus_j_trapper_sable.text: The hunters say that beyond the far portage, up at the headwaters, there are black sables, each pelt worth a cow. But it is a month's journey, and the forest folk there don't like strangers.
ev.rus_j_trapper_sable.go.success: You came back with forty sables. Merchants practically fought over them at market.
ev.rus_j_trapper_sable.go.failure: The forest folk burned your winter hut. You came back with nothing.
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.title: Blizzard
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.text: A blizzard has blown up in the forest: you can't see two paces ahead and your ski track is gone. The winter hut is three miles off, or maybe six; you can no longer tell.
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.dig: Dig into the snow by a fire and wait
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.dig.success: By morning the blizzard had passed. You came out unharmed.
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.dig.failure: The fire blew out around midnight. You lost toes to frostbite.
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.push.success: You came straight out at the hut, as if your feet knew the way.
ev.rus_j_trapper_blizzard.push.failure: You wandered until dawn and nearly froze.
ev.rus_j_bell.title: The Great Bell
ev.rus_j_bell.text: A monastery has ordered a great bell weighing hundreds of poods. The mould is buried in a pit by the river and the bronze is boiling in the furnace. If a bubble stays in the metal, the bell will crack at the first stroke.
ev.rus_j_bell.cast.success: They raised the bell to the belfry and struck it, and the sound rolled out for miles. The monks wept.
ev.rus_j_bell.cast.failure: The bell is cracked. You must remelt the bronze at your own expense.
ev.rus_j_bell.small: Offer a set of small bells instead
ev.rus_j_cannon_yard.title: The Cannon Yard
ev.rus_j_cannon_yard.text: At the Cannon Yard on the Neglinnaya they cast arquebuses and huge cannon for the sovereign's army. They need masters who know bronze. It is crown service: steady pay, but strict accounting.
ev.rus_j_cannon_yard.go: Join the Cannon Yard as a master
ev.rus_j_silver_spoons.title: Wooden Spoons
ev.rus_j_silver_spoons.text: At the prince's feast the retainers have had too much and grumble: "It's a poor life, eating with wooden spoons instead of silver!" Prince Vladimir hears every word.
ev.rus_j_silver_spoons.grumble.success: The prince had silver spoons made for the retinue: "With silver and gold I cannot win a retinue, but with a retinue I shall win silver and gold."
ev.rus_j_silver_spoons.grumble.failure: The prince frowned, and you were moved to the far end of the table.
ev.rus_j_silver_spoons.note: According to the Primary Chronicle, Vladimir Svyatoslavich had silver spoons made after his retainers grumbled. The chronicler has him say that a retinue is worth more than silver.
ev.rus_j_voevoda.title: A Hundred Men
ev.rus_j_voevoda.text: The commander noticed you on the last campaign and is giving you a hundred men. Now you answer for every one of them, and for making sure they don't run.
ev.rus_j_strelets_recruit.title: Musketeer Levy
ev.rus_j_strelets_recruit.text: The tsar is recruiting streltsy, foot soldiers armed with matchlocks. They get a yard in the musketeers' quarter, pay in money and grain, and the right to trade without tolls. The service is for life, and passes to your son.
ev.rus_j_strelets_stall.title: A Stall in the Quarter
ev.rus_j_strelets_stall.text: Pay is late again, and half the quarter is trading: rolls, boots, anything. A fellow strelets invites you to go halves on a stall by the Moskvoretsky gate.
ev.rus_j_portage.title: The Portage
ev.rus_j_portage.text: The river has run out. The boat must be hauled overland on log rollers through the forest to the next river, three days' work. The local men will do it for a fee.
ev.rus_j_ladya_owner.title: A Boat of Your Own
ev.rus_j_ladya_owner.text: An old owner is selling a sturdy planked boat with a sail, as he no longer travels the rivers himself. With it you could carry your own goods from portage to portage instead of hiring out to others.
ev.rus_j_love_letter.title: A Birch-Bark Letter
ev.rus_j_love_letter.text: The girl next door, red to her ears, asks you to scratch a letter on birch bark to a lad across town: "Why have you forgotten me? If I were dear to you, you would have come to me."
ev.rus_j_love_letter.lecture: Write it, but give her a lecture first
ev.rus_mv_kiev_north.title: To the Land Beyond the Forests
ev.rus_mv_kiev_north.text: Kiev is emptying: princes fight over it, and the Polovtsians burn villages right outside the town. People you know are moving north-east to the land of Vladimir, where it is quieter and the prince gives settlers land.
ev.rus_mv_kiev_north.stay: The graves of my forebears are here
ev.rus_mv_to_moscow.title: Moscow Beckons
ev.rus_mv_to_moscow.text: The prince of Moscow is gathering people: whoever settles on his land is spared tribute for several years. They say even the metropolitan now lives in Moscow rather than Vladimir.
ev.rus_mv_to_novgorod.title: To Lord Novgorod the Great
ev.rus_mv_to_novgorod.text: A merchant you know invites you to Novgorod: trade with foreign guests, silver flowing like a river, and a city that, they say, bows to no one. Any craft there will find buyers.
ev.rus_mv_vyvod.title: The Deportation
ev.rus_mv_vyvod.text: The sovereign has ordered Novgorod's merchants and boyars, thousands of families, "removed" and resettled in Muscovite towns, with Muscovites given their houses. Your name is on the list.
ev.rus_mv_vyvod.hide.success: They never found you. You live as a simple peasant now, but on your own land.
ev.rus_mv_vyvod.hide.failure: They found you and sent you off under guard, taking even what you had left.
ev.rus_mv_vyvod.note: After annexing Novgorod in 1478, Ivan III carried out mass deportations in the 1480s: thousands of Novgorod boyars, well-off townsmen and merchants were resettled elsewhere, and their estates handed to Muscovite servicemen.
ev.rus_mv_service_capital.title: Service in the Capital
ev.rus_mv_service_capital.text: You have been listed among the "Thousand" chosen servants of the sovereign: you will get an estate near the capital if you serve at court. Your Novgorod fields will be left without their master's eye.
ev.rus_mv_service_capital.stay: Ask to be excused and stay
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.title: "Putyata Baptised with the Sword"
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.text: Dobrynya and the captain Putyata have come from Kiev with a bishop. The idol of Perun is being dragged to the Volkhov, the people of the Trade Side have torn up the bridge, and across the river the houses of the stubborn are already burning.
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.baptize: Go into the river to be baptised
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.resist: Stand up for the old gods
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.resist.success: You slipped off into the forest and pray to Perun in secret. For now.
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.resist.failure: You were seized and plunged into the Volkhov along with everyone else.
ev.rus_r_novgorod_baptism.note: The baptism of Novgorod around 990 met resistance. The saying "Putyata baptised with the sword and Dobrynya with fire" comes from the late Joachim Chronicle, whose reliability is disputed.
ev.rus_r_volkhv.title: A Seer in the Market
ev.rus_r_volkhv.text: In the market a pagan seer is shouting that he knows the future: he promises to walk across the river as if on dry land and threatens disaster to all who bow to the new God. Half the town has gone over to him; only the prince and his retinue stand with the bishop.
ev.rus_r_volkhv.watch: Watch from the side to see how it ends
ev.rus_r_volkhv.note: Under 1071 the chronicle tells of a seer in Novgorod: the people sided with him, and Prince Gleb asked him whether he knew what would happen to him that day, then killed him with an axe. Seers also led risings in the Suzdal land in 1024 and 1071.
ev.rus_r_dvoeverie.title: Two Faiths
ev.rus_r_dvoeverie.text: A housewarming. The old women say you must carry the house spirit over from the old cottage, in a bast shoe with an ember from the stove, and treat him to porridge. The priest calls it devilry in his sermons.
ev.rus_r_dvoeverie.old_way: Invite the house spirit the old way
ev.rus_r_dvoeverie.priest: Call the priest to bless the house
ev.rus_r_jews_kiev.title: The Community's Letter
ev.rus_r_jews_kiev.text: The elders of the Jewish community by the Jews' Gate are writing a letter to fellow believers in distant cities, collecting silver to help a man who has fallen into debt and trouble. Under the letter go the names of everyone who gave.
ev.rus_r_jews_kiev.note: The 10th-century "Kievan Letter" in Hebrew, found in the Cairo Geniza, is a letter of recommendation from Kiev's Jewish community asking help for a man in debt. Kiev had a Jews' Gate and a Jewish quarter.
ev.rus_r_tatar_service.title: A Tatar in Service
ev.rus_r_tatar_service.text: You come from the service Tatars in the sovereign's pay. A clerk hints: accept baptism and you will get a bigger estate and a higher rank. Many have already been baptised, and the mullah in the quarter looks at them reproachfully.
ev.rus_r_tatar_service.keep: Keep the faith of your fathers
ev.rus_r_strigolniki.title: The Strigolniki
ev.rus_r_strigolniki.text: A defrocked deacon speaks quietly by the river: priests are ordained for bribes and give communion for money, and you can just as well confess to mother earth. Many listen to him, especially craftsmen.
ev.rus_r_strigolniki.note: The Strigolniki were a movement in Novgorod and Pskov in the late 14th and early 15th centuries that denounced the clergy's greed. Their leaders were executed in 1375, but the teaching lasted another half-century.
ev.rus_r_strigolniki_later.title: Summoned by the Archbishop
ev.rus_r_strigolniki_later.text: The archbishop is investigating the Strigolniki, and someone has named you. You are summoned to judgement: repent before everyone, or stand your ground.
ev.rus_r_strigolniki_later.firm.success: The archbishop waved his hand: "Foolish, not wicked." You were released.
ev.rus_r_strigolniki_later.firm.failure: You were excommunicated. Neighbours give your house a wide berth.
ev.rus_r_baptize_late.title: Be Baptised?
ev.rus_r_baptize_late.text: Almost everyone around you is baptised now. The priest reminds you that the unbaptised cannot be married in church or buried in the churchyard beside their own. Yet in the forest by the stream still stands a stone where people bring offerings.
ev.rus_r_late_vows.title: Vows in Old Age
ev.rus_r_late_vows.text: You are alone in the world and your strength is going. Many at your age enter a monastery with a gift: to live out their days in prayer, with someone to bury and remember them.
ev.rus_r_late_vows.world: Live out your days in the world
